metadata.title: The Impact of Family and Individual Factors on 4th Grade Students’ Self-Confidence in Reading Literacy Results from PIRLS 2016
metadata.venue: Proceedings of the International Scientific Conference. Volume II, May 28th-29th, 2021. 203-213

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: The study uses PIRLS 2016 Student and Home Questionnaire data for Grade 4 students from Latvia and seven Baltic Sea comparison countries (Denmark, Finland, Germany, Lithuania, Poland, Russian Federation, Sweden). The methodology section does not report whether PIRLS sampling/school weights or replicate weights were applied in the linear regression and correlation analyses, nor does it name any weight variables. Because the analysis is based on PIRLS questionnaire scales and reading achievement relationships, analysts should use the PIRLS-provided complex survey weights when conducting population-representative inference; however, this manuscript does not document that step. No PV-specific weighting is relevant here because the dependent variable is a self-confidence scale index rather than a PV-based achievement outcome.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: The dependent variable is students’ self-confidence in reading measured via a Likert-based Students Confident in Reading Scale index, and the paper reports linear regression R² and standardized regression coefficients rather than PV-based achievement modeling. The manuscript does not describe any missing-data rule (e.g., complete-case exclusion or imputation), which is a reporting gap because questionnaire items and derived scales typically require handling of missing responses. Without documentation, it is unclear whether missingness was excluded listwise or addressed through imputation, limiting reproducibility.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The analytic sample is Grade 4 students who participated in PIRLS 2016 and have responses available for the PIRLS Student and Home Questionnaire scales used to construct the dependent self-confidence index and the independent variables (Early Literacy Skills, Parents Like Reading, Students Like Reading, Time Students Spent Chatting, and Has PC/tablet and Internet). The paper states that it analyzed PIRLS 2016 data from Latvia and seven Baltic Sea comparison countries, but it does not report additional inclusion/exclusion criteria (e.g., specific missing-response handling, achievement reporting thresholds, or any complete-case rule).

main_findings.dataset_used: PIRLS 2016 Grade 4 Reading (Students Confident in Reading Scale)
main_findings.performance_metrics: Per-country R² (self-confidence ~ reading achievement): Latvia 0.17, Denmark 0.25, Finland 0.18, Germany 0.16, Lithuania 0.22, Poland 0.16, Russian Federation 0.17, Sweden 0.17. Per-country R² (self-confidence ~ all independent variables): Latvia 0.26, Denmark 0.32, Finland 0.24, Germany 0.20, Lithuania 0.29, Poland 0.24, Russian Federation 0.27, Sweden 0.24. Significant standardized regression coefficients reported in Table 3 (e.g., Reading achievement beta ranges ~0.29–0.40; Students like reading beta ~0.17–0.25; Early literacy skills beta ~0.06–0.22; Parents like reading beta ~0–0.10; Time spent chatting beta ~0.01–0.06).
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using PIRLS 2016 Grade 4 Reading the study leveraged reading achievement, students like reading, early literacy skills, parents like reading, and time spent chatting to predict students’ self-confidence in reading, finding that reading achievement was the strongest predictor across all comparison countries and that adding family/home and individual factors increased explained variance by roughly ~10 percentage points in Latvia, Poland, and the Russian Federation. This indicates that strengthening early literacy and fostering positive reading attitudes at home may complement achievement-focused interventions to improve students’ reading self-confidence, though the study reports associations from linear regression rather than causal effects.

data.outcome_summary: The study analyzes PIRLS 2016 Grade 4 data from Latvia and seven Baltic Sea comparison countries (Denmark, Finland, Germany, Lithuania, Poland, Russian Federation, Sweden) to explain variation in students’ self-confidence in reading measured by the Students Confident in Reading Scale index. Using linear regression, the authors report that reading achievement is closely related to self-confidence, with R² values around 0.16–0.25 across countries (highest in Denmark at 0.25). When all independent variables are added (reading achievement plus students’ reading enjoyment, early literacy skills, parents’ reading enjoyment, time spent chatting, and home PC/tablet with internet), R² increases to about 0.20–0.32, with the largest gains in Latvia, Poland, and the Russian Federation (about +0.10). The paper does not report missing-data handling or whether PIRLS complex survey weights were applied, limiting generalizability and reproducibility. The results are correlational/associational and should not be interpreted as causal impacts.
